title: JenaClimateForecasting
body:
P22 - EC417 Introduction to Machine Intelligence
M Sanjhay Baargav (623147)
Trinesh Kumar (623138)
notes: Introduce the team and the forecasting question. 20 seconds.

title: Forecasting task
body:
120 hourly observations predict temperature 24 hours ahead
Primary metric: MAE in degrees Celsius
Auxiliary forecast horizons: 1, 6 and 12 hours
notes: Explain forecast origin, history and target. 25 seconds.

title: Chronological data split
body:
420,551 raw observations
Train: 2009-2014
Validation: 2015
Final test: 2016

title: Preprocessing without future information
body:
Hourly bins end at their timestamp
Wind components replace direction and speed
Fill gaps within each period
Fit normalization using training years
Create windows after splitting
notes: Explain -9999 sentinels, missing-target exclusion, and split-boundary tests. 30 seconds.

title: Baselines and GRU
body:
Persistence repeats the latest temperature
Ridge uses the flattened 120-hour window
GRU uses 24 hidden units and four outputs
Validation chooses penalties and checkpoints
notes: Reference: https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.1078. Explain gates, not just the name. 35 seconds.

title: Calendar feature experiment
body:
Add four inputs to the GRU
Sine and cosine of hour
Sine and cosine of position within the year
Keep data, seeds and training rules fixed
notes: The input parameter count increases slightly. Both GRUs already share the auxiliary horizon outputs. 30 seconds.

title: Measured 24-hour test results
body: Calendar features reduced GRU 24-hour test MAE by 0.094 degrees C (4.3%).
notes: Read MAE means and standard deviations. Baselines are deterministic. No significance claim. 40 seconds.

title: Error versus forecast horizon
body: Longer horizons test a different prediction difficulty
notes: Use the measured horizon chart. Error bars in the report show seed variability. 30 seconds.

title: Forecast errors and limits
body:
Largest calendar-GRU monthly MAE: 2.901 C in month 1
One station and one test year
Overlapping windows share weather conditions
Weather causes of extreme errors remain hypotheses
notes: The calendar GRU's largest monthly mean error occurs in month 1 (2.901 C across 601 forecast origins). For seed 17, the largest stored error is 11.44 C at 2016-05-23 19:00:00: actual 13.19 C versus prediction 24.63 C. Rapid temperature changes and missing spatial weather information are possible explanations, not verified causes. 35 seconds.

title: Reproduction and next steps
body:
python run_project.py
Review the code and explain the results
Next: variable ablation and new test years
AI assistance: OpenAI Codex, disclosed in the report
notes: Show the README, tests and source modules. Explain team verification and commit-history requirements. 25 seconds.
